implementation_state: A provider names a ProviderClientProfile (auto, native, claude_code, codex) that decides both the fingerprint Zroutery presents upstream and which of the inbound client's own headers may travel with it. Auto detects the client from the leading token of `x-zroutery-client` (else the User-Agent), and falls back to the native identity rather than inventing a fingerprint. The legacy `impersonate_claude_code` boolean migrates to the Claude Code profile in AppConfig::normalize, one-way and idempotent, and is skipped on serialisation. Forwarding is an allowlist per profile, resolved once per attempt into a ClientIdentity and applied after the fabricator so a real client header beats a fabricated one; authentication and framing headers are excluded by the allowlist and again by PASSTHROUGH_DENIED. prompt_cache_key survives the /v1/responses dialect round trip. The failure authority also gained QuotaExhausted for an exhausted upstream budget pool, distinct from the local OverBudget.
required_gates: Profile resolution and one-way legacy migration
Per-profile upstream header fingerprint, exclusive between profiles
Allowlisted client-header forwarding that never touches authentication
prompt_cache_key survives the Responses dialect round trip
unblock_condition: Not blocked; the capability is complete and every gate passes.
notes: Forwarding is an allowlist, not a general passthrough; a header the client really sent is forwarded only if the resolved profile names it.
